answer: Each identity is admitted only after evaluating a challenge-bound chain of sequential modular squarings, where each result feeds the next; a Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check the work cheaply. GPUs cannot parallelize one chain, so cloning identities does not remove each clone’s physical time bottleneck, though separate chains can run concurrently. This is no fable: even a sparrow’s whisper cannot make the computation finish sooner.
